## Summary The kernel fusion tier now reports in the same shape as the compute tier. Fusion Data tables use compute's 10 columns and are built from the same perf-report rows and helpers. `analysis.json` gains a `fusion_optimizations[]` tier sorted on the same `impact.mid` key as compute. Two scoring bugs are fixed along the way: fusion time no longer extrapolates from the first instance, and compute now skips fusion-covered rows by op key instead of by kernel name. The fusion Identification now names the module, its caller and the launch path of each op. 21 files, +1994 / -650. ## Why | Pain point | Old | New | |---|---|---| | Fusion tables don't match compute | `Kernel / Type / Duration (us) / Perf model`, one row per kernel, first instance only | Compute's 10 columns, one row per launching op and args, from the same perf-report row | | Fusion time is overstated | First instance's kernel time × `instance_count`. A module whose instances differ in shape gets every instance scored at the largest shape | Sum of the real kernel time over every instance | | Wrong perf row | Lookup on kernel name + first input shape, with prefix matching. One GEMM or elementwise kernel serves many ops | Lookup on `perf_row_key`: op name + args + process/thread, the perf report's own grouping | | Same time counted in both tiers | Compute flagged rows whose kernel name appeared in the first instance of a HIGH candidate, so rows from later instances slipped through | Compute flags a row when its `perf_row_key` is one of the HIGH candidate's op keys | | No fusion in `analysis.json` | `findings()` walked `tier=compute` only; a test asserted the fusion key was absent | `fusion_optimizations[]`, same task shape as compute, sorted on `impact.mid` | | Fusion `operation` carried the severity badge | `"🔴 P1: Unfused Attention"`, the raw heading | `"Unfused Attention"`, the bare name, like compute | | Identification didn't say where the kernels came from | Described the kernel sequence only | Names the module, its parent and call site, and the launch path of each op | | `—` op_row cells inflated compute | A `—` cell (fusion-flagged row) back-filled to `pct_e2e × 0.30` | A `—` cell scores 0. The back-fill only runs when a block has no op_row marker at all | ## Architecture ``` trace.json ─► TreePerf (tree_perf.py) │ event_process_thread_names() shared process/thread naming ▼ perf_report_csvs/unified_perf_summary.csv │ utils/orchestrator_prepare.py _extract_standalone_fusion_candidates / _extract_comparative_fusion_candidates OpResolver.fields(uid) kernel ─► launching op + perf_row_key _group_ops() one entry per op+args, summed over every instance ▼ category_data/fusion_candidates.json candidate.ops[] (ops_trace1/2[] comparative) │ category_analyses/kernel_fusion_analysis.py compute_fusion_impact_estimates() _standalone_estimate / _comparative_estimate impact_score on summed group time build_rows() format_args, calculate_efficiency, entry_point (compute's helpers) estimate.op_keys main() ─► high_confidence_op_keys (HIGH confidence only) ▼ category_data/kernel_fusion_metrics.json ─────────────┐ high_confidence_op_keys │ ▼ │ analysis_utils.run_category_analysis() │ build_operation_metrics() │ _load_fusion_op_keys + perf_row_key(row) │ ─► fusion_flagged ─► op_row cell "—" (score 0) ▼ ▼ kernel-fusion-analyzer.md (sub-agent) compute analyzers (sub-agents) ▼ ▼ system_findings/kernel_fusion_findings.md category_findings/_findings.md └──────────────────┬──────────────────┘ ▼ analysis.md (templates/analysis_template.md) validation_utils: _iter_candidate_blocks(tier), _validate_fusion_data_tables() ▼ standalone only post_processing/analysis_json.py render_analysis_json() AnalysisMdParser.findings("compute") ─► TaskGrouper(compute) ─► compute_optimizations[] AnalysisMdParser.findings("fusion") ─► TaskGrouper(fusion) ─► fusion_optimizations[] ▼ analysis.json (candidate_schema: ComputeTask/ComputeMember, FusionTask/TaskMember) ▼ Hyperloom _analysis_json.load_report_tasks() reads compute_optimizations[] only, unchanged ``` ## Before and after All samples are illustrative: shapes are symbolic, kernel names and launcher paths are placeholders, and bandwidth peaks are written as ``. The example is a vision attention module with two shape variants (120 large instances and 60 small ones), which is exactly the case the old time extrapolation got wrong. ### Fusion block in `analysis.md` (standalone) **Before** ```markdown #### 🔴 P1: Unfused Attention (370.53 ms, 180 instances) **Identification:** The `Attention` module repeats 180 times inside the encoder layers. Each call launches a GEMM, then a softmax, then a second GEMM, and none of these kernels is a fused attention kernel. **Data:** | Kernel | Type | Duration (us) | Perf model | |--------|------|--------------|------------| | gemm_kernel_A... | GEMM | 356.6 | Yes | | softmax_fwd_kernel | Unknown | 1151.5 | No | | gemm_kernel_B... | GEMM | 550.4 | Yes | **Impact estimate:** ``` **After** ```markdown #### 🔴 P1: Unfused Attention **Identification:** The `Attention` module runs 180 times, called from its parent `EncoderLayer` at `model/encoder.py(NNN): forward`. The batched matrix multiplies and the attention-mask add are launched from `model/attention.py(NNN): forward`, and the softmax is launched from `torch/nn/functional.py(NNN): softmax`. This candidate was surfaced because each instance runs a GEMM → softmax → GEMM kernel sequence with no fused attention kernel anywhere in the module subtree. **Data:** | Operation | Args | Kernel Path | Kernel Name | Time (ms) | %E2E | Count | FLOPS/Byte | Efficiency | Bound | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | aten::bmm | (H,S,D) bf16
(H,D,S) bf16 | model/attention.py(NNN): forward | gemm_kernel_A... | 40.460 | 4.45 | 120 | 62.46 | 49.39% of TB/s | memory-bound | | aten::_softmax | (H,S,S) bf16 | torch/nn/functional.py(NNN): softmax | softmax_fwd_kernel(H,S,D) bf16 | model/attention.py(NNN): forward | gemm_kernel_B... | 55.056 | 6.06 | 120 | 62.46 | 36.51% of TB/s | memory-bound | | aten::bmm | (h,s,D) bf16
(h,D,s) bf16 | model/attention.py(NNN): forward | gemm_kernel_C... | 0.356 | 0.04 | 60 | 2.41 | 0.05% of TB/s | memory-bound | | aten::add | (1,h,s,s) bf16
(1,1,s,s) bf16 | model/attention.py(NNN): forward | elementwise_kernel... | 0.555 | 0.06 | 120 | 0.24 | 0.01% of TB/s | memory-bound | | aten::_softmax | (h,s,s) bf16 | torch/nn/functional.py(NNN): softmax | softmax_warp_fwd_kernel... | 0.295 | 0.03 | 60 | — | — | — | | aten::bmm | (h,s,s) bf16
(h,s,D) bf16 | model/attention.py(NNN): forward | gemm_kernel_C... | 0.385 | 0.04 | 60 | 2.41 | 0.05% of TB/s | memory-bound | **Resolution:** Call a vendor library's fused attention if one exists; otherwise write a custom fused kernel. **Impact estimate:** - Low end impact_score: 11.58 - High end impact_score: 15.45 ``` What changed: - **Heading** loses the `(ms, instances)` suffix, matching compute headings. - **Identification** names the module and its caller, then the launch path of each op from the Data rows. That tells a reader where a fused kernel would plug in. - **Group time** is 250.81 ms (the Time column summed), not 370.53 ms. The old number took the first, large-shape instance and multiplied it by all 180. The impact mid drops from 19.97 to 13.52 as a result. - **Softmax** turns out to be two thirds of the group. The old table showed it only as "Perf model: No". - **Labels** are Identification / Data / Resolution / Impact estimate. Fusion blocks have no Reasoning for Slowdown, because the reason is always the same: intermediates round-trip through HBM between separate kernels. - **`detail_estimate`** carries `mid` (compute and fusion alike). ### Comparative fusion block (md only) **Before** ```markdown **Trace1 kernels:** | Kernel | Type | Duration (us) | |--------|------|--------------| | moe_sort_kernel | Unknown | 120.0 | | moe_gemm1_kernel | Unknown | 480.0 | | moe_gemm2_kernel | Unknown | 480.0 | | moe_sum_kernel | Unknown | 80.0 | **Trace2 kernels:** | Kernel | Type | Duration (us) | |--------|------|--------------| | fused_moe_kernel_... | Unknown | 800.0 | ``` **After** (Efficiency and Bound on Trace 2 are `—` because the traces run on different platforms) ```markdown **Trace 1** (E2E 1.26 ms): | Operation | Args | Kernel Path | Kernel Name | Time (ms) | %E2E | Count | FLOPS/Byte | Efficiency | Bound | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | lib::moe_sort | (T,K) bf16
(E,K,N) bf16 | ... | moe_sort_kernel | 0.120 | 9.52 | 1 | 0.49 | ... | memory-bound | | lib::moe_gemm1 | (T,K) bf16
(E,K,N) bf16 | ... | moe_gemm1_kernel | 0.480 | 38.10 | 1 | — | — | — | | ... | **Trace 2** (E2E 0.80 ms): | Operation | Args | Kernel Path | Kernel Name | Time (ms) | %E2E | Count | FLOPS/Byte | Efficiency | Bound | |---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---| | lib::fused_moe | (T,K) bf16
(E,K,N) fp8 | ... | fused_moe_kernel_... | 0.800 | 100.00 | 1 | — | — | — | ``` The comparative score is unchanged (it already summed every instance). `analysis.json` stays standalone-only, so comparative changes are md only. ### `analysis.json` **Before:** no fusion key. ```json { "report_info": { ... }, "compute_optimizations": [ ... ] } ``` **After:** `fusion_optimizations[]` is always emitted (`[]` when there are no fusion blocks). A task has compute's task fields. `operation` is the heading with the severity badge and `P:` stripped, as for compute. Members have compute's member fields minus `impact_score`, since fusion has no per-row score. ```json "fusion_optimizations": [ { "priority": 1, "operation": "Unfused Attention", "identification": "The `Attention` module runs 180 times, called from its parent `EncoderLayer` at `model/encoder.py(NNN): forward`. ...", "reasoning": null, "resolution": "Call a vendor library's fused attention ...", "prose_truncated": false, "impact": {"mid": 13.52, "low": 11.58, "high": 15.45}, "members": [ { "kernel_launcher_path": "model/attention.py(NNN): forward", "library": null, "category": null, "analysis_md_rank": "P1", "kernel_name": ["gemm_kernel_A..."], "args_shapes": ["(H,S,D)", "(H,D,S)"], "args_datatypes": ["bf16", "bf16"], "time_ms": 40.46, "count": 120, "pct_e2e": 4.45, "flops_per_byte": 62.46, "efficiency_percent": 49.39, "efficiency_peak_value": "", "efficiency_peak_unit": "TB/s", "bound": "memory-bound" }, { "kernel_launcher_path": "torch/nn/functional.py(NNN): softmax", "kernel_name": ["softmax_fwd_kernel", "confidence": "high", "affected_gpu_kernels": ["gemm_kernel_A...", "..."], ...} ], "high_confidence_kernel_map": {"gemm_kernel_A...": "", "softmax_fwd_kernel...": ""} ``` **After** ```json "impact_estimates": [ { "operation": "", "confidence": "high", "time_ms": 250.805, ..., "rows": [{"operation": "aten::bmm", "args": "...", "kernel_path": "...", "kernel_name": "...", "time_ms": "40.460", "pct_e2e": "4.45", "count": 120, "flops_per_byte": "62.46", "efficiency": "49.39% of TB/s", "bound": "memory-bound"}, ...], "op_keys": [["aten::bmm", "((H, S, D), (H, D, S))", "('c10::BFloat16', 'c10::BFloat16')", "()", "('', '')", "", "
